l: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: This document is a collection of twelve Sherlock Holmes cases narrated or framed by Dr. John Watson, following Holmes’s investigations from Baker Street through London and the countryside. Holmes’s powers of disguise, observation, deduction, and occasional moral judgment drive each story, while Watson assists, records events, and often provides the human perspective. It begins with the King of Bohemia seeking recovery of a compromising photograph from Irene Adler. Holmes locates it, but Adler recognizes and outwits him, leaves with her husband Godfrey Norton, and becomes the woman whose wit defeats Holmes. In the Red-Headed League, Holmes exposes a fake employment scheme designed to clear Jabez Wilson’s shop while John Clay tunnels toward a bank. He next proves that James Windibank invented the fiancé Hosmer Angel to keep Mary Sutherland’s income in the family. The middle cases range from murder and inherited menace to mistaken identity and theft. Holmes clears James McCarthy by uncovering John Turner’s confession in the Boscombe Valley killing. He tries too late to save John Openshaw from the K. K. K., though he identifies the men pursuing the family papers. He reveals that beggar Hugh Boone is actually Neville St. Clair, hiding a profitable double life. The blue carbuncle is traced through a Christmas goose to James Ryder, whom Holmes releases after his confession. At Stoke Moran, Holmes discovers that Dr. Grimesby Roylott used a snake to kill Julia Stoner and endanger Helen; the snake kills Roylott instead. Later, Holmes investigates Victor Hatherley’s severed thumb and identifies Colonel Lysander Stark’s hydraulic press as part of a counterfeiting operation. He solves Hatty Doran’s apparent wedding disappearance by finding that she has reunited with her presumed-dead husband, Francis Hay Moulton. In the Beryl Coronet affair, Holmes clears Arthur Holder and shows that Mary Holder aided Sir George Burnwell’s theft. Finally, at the Copper Beeches, Holmes and Watson help Violet Hunter uncover Alice Rucastle’s imprisonment by her father, who used Hunter to impersonate her and control her inheritance. Across the collection, apparent scandals, crimes, disappearances, and mysteries are resolved through Holmes’s reconstruction of concealed motives and events, though some wrongdoers escape legal punishment or tragedy cannot be prevented.

l: Sherlock Holmes, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: Sherlock Holmes is a consulting and professional detective, described by Watson as a reasoning and observing machine and a specialist in crime. From Baker Street, where he has chambers and lodgings and is closely associated with Dr. John Watson, he conducts investigations chiefly for the love of his art rather than wealth. His central methods are disciplined observation, deduction before theorising, examination of physical traces, disguises, and prolonged thought. He is energetic, generally successful, and regarded as a last court of appeal, although his methods may be theoretical and fantastic. He has extraordinary observational and incisive reasoning powers, plays the violin, uses a black clay pipe, keeps newspaper cuttings, and has Bohemian habits; he also habitually uses cocaine, alternating it with ambition. The record unfolds through cases in which Holmes repeatedly converts apparently minor details into solutions. In the Irene Adler matter, he identifies the King of Bohemia, locates the hidden photograph through a staged fire alarm, but finds that Adler has anticipated him; he retains her photograph as his reward. He exposes the Red-Headed League as a diversion for a bank tunnel and captures John Clay. For Mary Sutherland, he proves that James Windibank created the Hosmer Angel deception. In Boscombe Valley, he clears James McCarthy by identifying John Turner and privately preserving Turner’s confession. After John Openshaw’s death, Holmes traces the threatening gang to the Lone Star and seeks to warn its captain. He resolves Neville St. Clair’s supposed disappearance by removing Hugh Boone’s disguise, follows the blue carbuncle through a goose supply chain to James Ryder, and releases Ryder after obtaining his confession. He uncovers Dr. Grimesby Roylott’s snake-based murder scheme at Stoke Moran, identifies a coining gang near Eyford, and explains Hatty Doran’s disappearance by tracing Francis Hay Moulton. He restores the stolen coronet gems and establishes Arthur Holder’s innocence through disguise and physical evidence. Finally, responding to Violet Hunter’s appeal at the Copper Beeches, he deduces that she was meant to impersonate Alice Rucastle, exposes Alice’s imprisonment and escape route, and resolves the remaining mystery through Mrs. Toller’s account. Throughout, Watson is his friend, colleague, assistant, witness, and chronicler.

l: Dr. Watson, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: Dr. Watson is a married medical practitioner and physician in civil practice in London, living near Paddington Station after having shared rooms with Sherlock Holmes at Baker Street. A veteran of the Afghan campaign who carries an army revolver and bears a jezail bullet in a limb, he is Holmes’s longtime friend, trusted companion, colleague, medical adviser, and chronicler. His marriage separates him socially from Holmes, but he repeatedly visits or travels with him, records his cases, and narrates their investigations. Across the records, Watson begins by observing Holmes’s deductions and agreeing to assist in the operation at Briony Lodge, where he follows instructions, throws a smoke-rocket, and despite misgivings about Irene Adler remains loyal to Holmes. He then acts as listener, observer, and armed partner in cases including the Red-Headed League bank ambush, Mary Sutherland’s interview, the Boscombe Valley inquiry, the Openshaw investigation, Neville St. Clair’s disappearance, the blue carbuncle, and the danger at Stoke Moran. He often admits that he cannot see what Holmes sees, initially misses significant details, or waits for Holmes’s explanation; nevertheless, he carefully records testimony, evidence, newspaper reports, conversations, and outcomes. Watson’s medical role is also central. He searches for Isa Whitney, treats Victor Hatherley after the loss of his thumb, and later treats the injured Mr. Rucastle. He introduces Hatherley’s case to Holmes and is described as the hydraulic engineer’s patient’s companion. In dangerous investigations he carries his revolver, keeps watch, helps protect Helen Stoner, and ultimately shoots a dog to save Rucastle while assisting Holmes in freeing a prisoner at the Copper Beeches. From Baker Street consultations through journeys to Boscombe Valley, Fairbank, Stoke Moran, and Winchester, Watson remains Holmes’s dependable collaborator and the written recorder of their adventures.

l: Irene Adler, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: Irene Adler is a well-known adventuress, former contralto and concert singer, trained actress, and woman born in New Jersey in 1858. She performed at La Scala, lived in Warsaw during a lengthy visit by the King, and later lives at Briony Lodge in London. Wronged by the King of Bohemia, she holds compromising letters and a photograph of herself with him, intending the photograph as protection if he marries another woman. She drives out daily, has one male visitor, and marries the man she loves, Godfrey Norton, at the Church of St. Monica. When Holmes stages a fight and false fire alarm at Briony Lodge to locate the concealed photograph, she recognizes his disguise but lets him expose its hiding place behind a sliding panel. She then flees England with Norton, retains the incriminating photograph, and leaves another photograph for the King.

l: the King of Bohemia, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: The hereditary King of Bohemia, also Grand Duke of Cassel-Felstein, is engaged to Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen but fears exposure of his past relationship with Irene Adler. Disguised as Count Von Kramm, he employs Sherlock Holmes after failed searches and burglary attempts. He accompanies Holmes to Briony Lodge, believes the photograph has been left behind, and gratefully permits Holmes to keep it.

l: Baker Street, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
s: Baker Street is the location of Sherlock Holmes’s rooms and lodgings, including 221B, and a recurring base for his work with Dr. Watson. Visitors come there for help, including the King, Alexander Holder, Violet Hunter, Henry Baker, and James Windibank. Holmes keeps books and case evidence there, receives notes and telegrams, investigates the blue carbuncle, and discusses or explains cases after expeditions. It is also a place of confrontation: Holmes locks Windibank inside briefly, then confronts James Ryder and obtains his confession. From early visits and invitations through meetings before and after an arrest, it remains the place to which Holmes and Watson return, including for breakfast, and where new cases begin with Holder’s arrival and Hunter’s urgent telegram.
